title: Companies with high forensic risk scores have underperformed
summary: US companies over $1B that scored 80 or higher on the Hudson Labs Forensic Risk Score in May 2026 fell 25.9% at the median over the next six months. The…
body_markdown:
Companies with a high Hudson Labs Forensic Risk Score have underperformed the market over the past six months and the past year. We grouped US companies with a market cap over **$1B** by the score they had at the start of each period and tracked their share prices from there.


Of the **2,049** companies in the six-month test, 65 had a score of 80 or higher on May 6, 2026. By the November 6 close the median stock in that group was down **25.9%** , while the median **$1B** + company was up **0.3%** . **That is a gap of 26.2 percentage points in six months.** The median company with a score under 40 was up **3.3%** .


## The same pattern over one year


The one-year test covers **1,807** companies grouped by their score on November 6, 2025. The 55 that scored 80 or higher fell **5.0%** on average over the following year, while the average **$1B** + company rose **13.8%** . **That is a gap of 18.8 percentage points.** Returns were lower in each higher score band.

Of the 65 companies that scored 80 or higher in May, 46 were down six months later. The mean for the group is less negative than the median because a few stocks rose a lot. The best one was up **275%** and the worst was down **95%** .

## The November 5 selloff


High scores also fell harder on a bad day. On Thursday November 5, 2026 the median **$1B** + company lost **3.1%** . The median company that had scored 80 or higher in May lost **6.4%** , and 59 of the 65 were down.


## How we ran it


Scores are point in time, so each company is grouped by the score it had on the start date. Returns are share price changes to the close on the end date. The one-year test leaves out companies that were delisted during the period. Past performance does not predict future returns.
